title: Recover, Discover, Plan: Learning Skills and Concepts from Robot Failures
title_zh: 恢复、发现与规划：从机器人失败中学习技能与概念
abstract: Intelligent robots should not only recover from failures, but also acquire the abstract knowledge needed to avoid them in the future. While reinforcement learning can learn reactive recovery behaviors, training a separate policy for every distinct failure mode is highly inefficient. We introduce Recovery-Driven Synthesis of Relational Concepts (ReSYNC), an approach that progressively discovers and refines state abstractions (relational predicates) from failure-recovery experience to support abstract planning. ReSYNC jointly learns skills and concepts through an incremental dual-learning process. In the skill-learning phase, the robot uses reinforcement learning to recover from failures seen in training tasks. In the concept-learning phase, it discovers relational predicates and refines its abstract planning model to explain and generalize the learned recovery behaviors. Across four simulated domains, ReSYNC outperforms strong baselines by over 50% on unseen long-horizon problems and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer for non-prehensile manipulation.

editorial.selection_reason: 从失败经历中先学习恢复技能，再发明能解释这些技能的关系谓词，把局部恢复转化为对新任务的全局失败规避。
